messages.author: cc9ad6130d21e6c8
messages.subject: R encountered a fatal error
parts:
Hello,

Since yesterday I'm having problems to run my simulation. I have no idea where the problem is coming from because, sometimes the simulation runs well, but most of the time it is returning an error inside one of my functions, and after sometime it crashes the R so that I have to restart the session. It's even strange that sometimes I get finished arrivals even with the error message. Any idea?

I shared the code so you can also check.

Thanks,

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] R encountered a fatal error
parts:
2017-11-23 9:29 GMT+01:00 Victor Hugo Nassau Batista
<victor.hu...@gmail.com>:

> Hello,
>
> Since yesterday I'm having problems to run my simulation. I have no idea
> where the problem is coming from because, sometimes the simulation runs
> well, but most of the time it is returning an error inside one of my
> functions, and after sometime it crashes the R so that I have to restart the
> session. It's even strange that sometimes I get finished arrivals even with
> the error message. Any idea?

The error I'm getting is pretty much self-explanatory:

Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) :
FLT_UL_1: release: not previously seized

It means that there's a path in your model in which an arrival may
reach a release of a resource (FLT_UL_1 in this case) without seizing
it before. And this should NOT happen, so you'll have to revise and
fix your model.

On the other hand, it seems that the crash is a consequence of the
latter, and emerges after multiple runs, so I'd say that it is not
important. I have to check and fix it though.

Iñaki

described on the other topic. Somehow the arrival is jumping some
steps of the process.

I'm reviewing the code in order to get around this problem, but I'm
also finding another things concerning the shuttle process. I'll
comment on that topic if I get to the point I cannot solve it.

Thank you for the help Inaki!

without a previous seize in your model, therefore it may be a bug. In
fact, disabling preemption solves the error and the crash. So it seems
a preemption problem, but we would need a smaller reproducible example
to delimit the issue. Let's see...

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] R encountered a fatal error
parts:
I see the problem: please note that your shuttle MUST be
NON-preemptive. Otherwise, the "trick" of setting the capacity up and
down to get a delayed release does not work. This is because if an
entity seizes a preemptive resource and decrements the capacity by
one, that entity is automatically preempted! So if you set the
"Shuttle" resource as "preemptive=FALSE", everything just works fine.

As a side effect, we have discovered a bug, because after preemption
happens, that entity should stop instead of continuing executing
activities. So every cloud has a silver lining...

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] R encountered a fatal error
parts:
Yesterday I made some modifications on the code. 
I turned off the functions to change the capacity of the shuttle and it started to work ok. But when I set the shuttles to be preemptive, the problem started again, which comes to confirm your observation.
I'll try your suggestion today and I though about a different approach to the delayed release. Instead of changing the capacity with a function, I simply put the wayback ("slave") trajectory to seize and release a shuttle and driver instead. I will elaborate it on the other topic later.

Thank you very much Inaki!
